test something to see whether it works

items.s: The study ____ ten people with advanced retinitis pigmentosa.
The virus had been ____ so that it could carry instructions to the cells.
Six of the ten patients ____ an important improvement in light sensitivity.
One serious problem ____ during an injection.
The results of the study, ____ in October 2026, offer some hope.

tfn.s: More than half of the patients showed a clear improvement in sensitivity to light.
tfn.why: The text says: "Six of the ten patients showed an important improvement in how sensitive they were to light."

tfn.s: The goggles will be available in shops next year.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say when the goggles might be sold.

tfn.s: The study was small, with ten patients.
tfn.why: The text says: "The study involved ten people with advanced retinitis pigmentosa."

tfn.s: The treatment allowed patients to recognise faces.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "the technology did not allow them to make out faces."

tfn.s: The virus was put into both eyes of each patient.
tfn.why: The text says doctors put a virus "into one eye".

to bring something back to how it was before

focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word such as on or off. The small word changes the meaning, so learn the pair together.

items.s: The team wants to find ____ whether the treatment is safe.
The goggles turn pictures ____ light signals.
The researchers will carry ____ with a larger study.
People should not give ____ hope after one small trial.
It is hard to tell two similar objects ____ without clear vision.
News reports should not ____ the results of a small early trial.
Access to the new treatment is ____ to people who join a clinical trial.
The flood destroyed most of the village, and the ____ houses were repaired later.
The doctor said the pain was ____ and that the patient needed hospital care at once.
The problem was ____ within minutes, and the test carried on.
Walking in a ____ room is easier than in a place you have never visited.

match.d: find a way past a difficulty
small, and not claiming to be impressive

items.s: By the time the study ended, six patients ____ a meaningful improvement.

If the trial had included an untreated group, the researchers ____ the two groups.
Immediately after an injection, a serious event ____, but it was treated within minutes.

tfn.s: The treatment costs less than existing eye surgery.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not compare the cost with other treatments.

tfn.s: Patients who practised more with the goggles generally performed better.
tfn.why: The text says: "Those who spent more time learning to use the goggles generally performed better."

tfn.s: The study appeared in the New England Journal of Medicine.
tfn.why: The text says it was "published in the New England Journal of Medicine in October 2026".

tfn.s: The trial included an untreated comparison group.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "had no untreated comparison group."

tfn.s: More participants showed some increase in light sensitivity than showed a clinically meaningful one.
tfn.why: Seven of the ten showed some increase, but only six showed a clinically meaningful improvement.

focus.note: Check what follows the gap: some of these verbs take an object, and some take a how-clause or another preposition.

items.s: These cells may no longer function, making ____ of normal sight extremely difficult.

tfn.s: Everyone whose light sensitivity increased also reached the level the study counted as a clinically meaningful improvement.
tfn.why: Seven participants had increased sensitivity, but only six met the study's level.

tfn.s: The optogenetic approach could in principle help people whose severe sight loss has different genetic causes.
tfn.why: The text says several causes of severe retinal degeneration "might be addressed through the same general mechanism".

tfn.s: Participants practised with the goggles at home during the study.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say where participants used the goggles.

tfn.s: The gene therapy was injected into each participant's better-seeing eye.
tfn.why: The text says it went into "the worse-seeing eye of each participant".

tfn.s: The treatment worked on cells that were still present after the photoreceptors had stopped working.
tfn.why: The photoreceptors may no longer function, yet other retinal cells remain relatively intact and are modified.

focus.note: At this level many phrasal verbs are figurative. Learn the whole unit and the particle that follows, such as aside, out, on or up.

items.s: Sceptics were quick to ____ aside the findings as too small to matter.
A small trial without a control group cannot ____ out the possibility that chance explains the result.
It is too early to say how the research will ____ out.
Patients should not ____ on a cure from a single small trial.
Larger studies are needed to ____ up these early claims.

speak.title: Role-play: choosing a headline
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You edit a newsletter for a charity that supports people with sight loss. You want a short, exciting headline about a small trial. Ask the writer what the study really showed, then decide together.

b.text: You've read about a small trial. It helped some people find objects, but it isn't a cure. Explain why the headline must be honest, and suggest a version you both like.

phrases: I'd like the headline to catch people's attention.
We shouldn't promise more than the study showed.
What if we say it's an early step?
I'm not sure that's fair to our readers.
Let's agree on a version we're both happy with.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: which headline did you choose, and why is it fair to readers?
